metadata.title: Two Notes That Pulse Into Silence
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: Two steady notes, almost the same pitch. Why does their combined sound pulse, loud and soft?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: Sound two steady notes at almost the same pitch, one at four hundred forty hertz and one at four hundred forty four hertz. The combined sound does not stay steady. It swells and fades, loud, then soft, then loud again. Where does that slow pulse come from?
beats.new_visual_element: Two stacked strip charts of pressure versus time at the listener, scrolling continuously: a teal sinusoid labeled 440 Hz on top, a crimson sinusoid labeled 444 Hz below, both starting in phase.

beats.narration_text: Each curve records the air pressure at the ear as time passes. The second note oscillates slightly faster, so its crests gradually pull ahead of the first note's crests. The two waves drift out of step, and then back into step, over and over.
beats.new_visual_element: Dashed vertical guides, scrolling with the charts, through instants where the crests line up (ink, labeled in step) and where crest meets trough (slate, labeled out of step). A small slate note says the frequency difference is exaggerated for visibility.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: two scrolling waves, in-step and out-of-step guides, exaggeration note

beats.narration_text: The ear receives the sum of the two waves. Where the crests line up, the waves reinforce, and the combined amplitude doubles, so the sound is loud. Where a crest meets a trough, the waves cancel, and the sound falls nearly silent.
beats.new_visual_element: The two component curves copy down and merge into a single black sum curve on a third axis, computed live as their point-by-point sum. Soft grey bands mark the scrolling regions of cancellation. The guides fade.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: two faint component waves above, black scrolling sum below with grey silence bands

beats.narration_text: The peaks of the sum trace out a slow envelope that swells and pinches at a steady rate. That rate is the beat frequency, and it equals the difference between the two frequencies. Four hundred forty four minus four hundred forty gives four hertz: four beats every second.
beats.new_visual_element: A gold dashed envelope hugging the sum's peaks, scrolling with it; a gold amplitude bar at the present instant that rises and falls with the envelope. Equation f_beat = |f2 - f1| = 444 Hz - 440 Hz = 4 Hz.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: faint components, sum with envelope, silence bands, amplitude bar, beat-frequency equation

beats.narration_text: Two steady tones produce one slow pulse, and its rate is set only by the gap between their frequencies. This is how a piano tuner works: as a string is tuned toward a reference tone, the beats slow down, and they vanish when the two frequencies match.
beats.new_visual_element: Summary line: BEAT FREQUENCY = DIFFERENCE OF THE TWO FREQUENCIES. The sum, envelope and amplitude bar keep pulsing.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: summary, equation, faint components, pulsing sum with envelope and amplitude bar
